Set up your safety in a few simple steps\nand we\u2019ll be ready when you need us.
We\u2019ll check on you if there\u2019s no activity
If you can\u2019t speak, let your card speak for you

You may not be able to ask for help, and your Emergency Card can help even when you can\u2019t: your details are always ready, responders can still help, anyone who finds it can view essential information, and it can make a real difference in critical moments. No personal unlock, no app installation.
A stronger safety network around you. Your Emergency Card can be used by police and officials, ambulance services, hospital staff and bystanders. More people informed means faster help for you.
Your Emergency Card, always up to date. If your details change, update your card: edit your information, set it as your lock screen, share it, download it as a PDF, or print it.

What a responder sees once they scan: your name and age, your blood group and allergies, your emergency contacts with a call button beside each, and your medical conditions, medications and other information.

How a responder uses your Emergency Card. One, they find the card. Two, they scan the QR code with their phone. Three, your emergency details appear. Four, they call your emergency contacts and get the information they need to assist you. No personal unlock, no app installation.
Ways to carry your card: on the back of your mobile, on your mobile lock screen, in your wallet, on your bike or scooter, in your car, or on your bag or luggage.
When your Emergency Card can help: an accident, a medical emergency, when you can\u2019t speak, when your phone is locked, or when you are found unable to respond.
How PUKAAR works: SOS gets you help in an emergency, Inactivity checks on you if you are not active for a while, and the Emergency Card speaks for you when you can’t.

When you can\u2019t speak, let your card speak for you. You don\u2019t need to use it during an emergency \u2014 someone helping you can scan it and get the details they need. Be prepared for any situation, because every second matters.
Let your loved ones\nknow you reached safely

Safe Arrival: set your expected arrival time and choose your trusted contact. PUKAAR keeps your loved ones informed only when needed — on night outs, while travelling, after late work, for students, and when home alone.

Set Expected Arrival Time — for example, you are in Pune at an event and expect to reach home around 1:00 AM. Your parents in Mumbai are notified only if you don’t reach home by then; they don’t need to know where you are or what you’re doing.
Choose Contact(s) — pick who PUKAAR should notify if you don’t confirm your arrival, or add a new contact. Here the daughter selects her mother in Mumbai, who won’t know she is out.
Review and Start — confirm your arrival time and the contacts to notify. PUKAAR will check on you at the set time, and if you don’t respond your contacts will be alerted with your live location.
Are you safe? At your expected arrival time you get a notification asking you to confirm: Yes, I’ve arrived, or I’ll take more time.
Extend Time — if she feels she’ll be delayed, she can extend by 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour or a custom time before the grace period.
Grace Period — after the extended time, a grace period starts, for example 30 minutes. No alerts yet: she may still be on the way.
Scenario 1, I’ve Arrived — she reaches home safely and taps I’ve Arrived on time. Safe arrival is confirmed and the journey closes; her mother and Amit are never informed because everything is fine.

Scenario 2, No response? After a short grace period, your trusted contacts are alerted with your live location so they can check on you. If there is no response from your end, your mother and Amit would be alerted with your live location.
See how PUKAAR can help in real-life situations.

Who is PUKAAR for? PUKAAR is for people who may be alone, away from home, travelling, or difficult to reach when something goes wrong. SOS when you need help right now, Inactivity when something may have happened and you don’t respond, Emergency Card when you can’t speak, and Safe Arrival when someone wants to know you arrived safely.
Students studying away from home in India — living in a hostel, PG or another city. Far from home, still within a safety layer.

Students studying abroad — thousands of kilometres away in an unfamiliar country, where family cannot reach them quickly and time zones make it hard to connect. When you can’t be there, PUKAAR can be there.
Working professionals away from home — living or working away from family, often returning late or travelling for work. Away from home, still connected to help.
Frequent business travellers — moving between cities, staying in hotels or working in unfamiliar places. Wherever work takes you, carry a safety layer with you.
People who spend a lot of time on the road — frequent riders, drivers, field workers, salespeople and daily commuters. More time on the road, more reason for a safety layer.
Women and teenage girls — going to college, work, parties, events or travelling late at night. Freedom to go, confidence to return safely.
Elderly and seniors — living independently or spending significant time alone. More independence, more reassurance.
Night-shift workers — travelling to or from work during late-night or early-morning hours. When the world is asleep, your safety layer stays awake.
Solo travellers — travelling alone in unfamiliar cities, destinations or surroundings. Travel alone, don’t face an emergency alone.
Outdoor and adventure enthusiasts — trekking, hiking, cycling, camping or exploring remote and unfamiliar places. Go farther, stay connected to help.
People whose families live far away — living in another city or country while their loved ones are far away. Distance shouldn’t mean less peace of mind.
Anyone living alone — without someone immediately nearby to notice when something goes wrong. Living alone doesn’t mean being alone in an emergency.

The simple PUKAAR connection: SOS, Inactivity, Emergency Card and Safe Arrival. Emergencies don’t come with a warning, and every second matters. PUKAAR is a safety layer for people who may not always have someone beside them.

How PUKAAR can help: real situations, real protection when it matters. SOS gets you help in an emergency, Inactivity checks on you, and the Emergency Card carries your information for when you can\u2019t speak.

SOS \u2014 in immediate danger? Press SOS and your trusted contacts are alerted with the information they need to help. Examples: road accident, unsafe cab or vehicle, being followed or threatened, serious medical emergency.

Inactivity \u2014 when someone should check on you. If there is no activity for your set time, PUKAAR can trigger a welfare check. Examples: living alone, travelling alone, studying in another city or country, on a trek, hike or outdoor journey.

Emergency Card \u2014 if you can\u2019t speak, let your card speak for you. Your Emergency Card gives responders instant access to your emergency information via a QR code. Examples: accident or unconscious, medical emergency, can\u2019t speak, phone locked, found unable to respond.

Be prepared for when it matters. Different situations, one solution: SOS when you are in immediate danger, Inactivity when someone should check on you, and the Emergency Card for when you can\u2019t speak.

A quiet phone can be the first sign of trouble. This is what happens when yours goes quiet.

PUKAAR runs three protections side by side: SOS for a life-threatening emergency, Help for when you need a hand without an ambulance, and Elderly Help for when your phone goes quiet. Each one alerts the trusted contacts you set up for it.
Press the SOS button on the home screen, or press the power button three times quickly. A five-second countdown follows, and you can cancel within it.
Not automatically. The nearest police station, ambulance and hospital are listed for your contacts along with 112, so calling is one tap away when it is needed.

Recording only starts when you trigger an alert. Elderly Help watches for ordinary phone activity without recording or sharing anything. During an SOS the audio is stored on the server every minute as evidence.
How PUKAAR Works, in the menu, walks through every step of each feature. Mock Drill lets you experience a full SOS or Help alert in five minutes.
Who is alerted when I press SOS?
All three trusted contacts receive the alert at the same moment.
Audio begins recording automatically, without opening anything.
What if I lose the phone?
Everything is saved to the cloud. The recording is uploaded every minute, so it survives losing the phone.
What is sent along with the alert?
Your details go with it: live location, battery level and your number are shared with the alert.
How do my contacts reach emergency services?
Emergency services are one tap away. The nearest police, ambulance and hospital are listed, along with 112.
Do I have to do anything after pressing SOS?
No. One press starts all of this at once. You do not have to do anything else.
How long is a quiet period?
You choose the window in Elderly Help — six, ten or twelve hours without activity are the usual choices.
The timer resets itself: unlocking the phone or opening any app starts the count again.
Am I warned before my contacts are?
No. PUKAAR tracks phone use silently in the background — you are not notified. Only your trusted contacts are alerted if there is no activity.
What happens if there is no phone activity?
Your trusted contacts receive a welfare alert on WhatsApp and through the High Alert app.
Inactivity, How It Works: if you are inactive for a long time, PUKAAR makes sure help reaches the right people.
Step 1 of 14, Set Inactivity Duration: choose 6, 12 or 18 hours, or a custom time. The default is 12 hours and you can change it anytime.
Step 2 of 14, Add Trusted Contacts: add up to 3 trusted contacts who will be alerted.
Step 3 of 14, Add Pre-saved Emergency Contacts: family, friends, a neighbour — these numbers are shared during an emergency.
Step 4 of 14, How Monitoring Works: PUKAAR runs in the background and watches for the app not being opened, no movement detected and no manual check-in.
Step 5 of 14, Soft Notification: at 50 percent of the set time with no activity, you get a gentle check-in notification. Just a reminder, no need to panic.
Step 6 of 14, Soft Alert: at 100 percent of the set time with still no activity, a soft alert goes to your primary trusted person.
Step 7 of 14, High Alert: after a further grace period, about an hour, a high alert with loud sound and vibration reaches the primary trusted person.
Step 8 of 14, If No Response in 1 Minute: the primary trusted person has one minute to respond.
Step 9 of 14, Alert Goes to 2nd and 3rd Contacts: the high alert is passed on to your second and third trusted contacts.
Step 10 of 14, Details They Receive: your number, live location, battery level, active status and each other’s details, along with your pre-saved emergency contacts.
Step 11 of 14, Nearby Emergency Services: the nearest police station, ambulance and hospital, plus 112 — all one tap away.
Step 12 of 14, They Call You First: if you respond the situation is handled; if you don’t, they act on every detail and option provided.

Step 13 of 14, What Trusted Contacts Receive: name and number, live location, battery level, network status, last active time, the full trusted contacts list, pre-saved emergency contacts and nearby emergency services.

Step 14 of 14, You Also Receive It: everything sent to your trusted contacts is sent to you too — location, details, device status, pre-saved help numbers, emergency services and the recording — along with whether each contact has received and read the alert.
Step 1, Trigger SOS: tap the SOS button, or press the power button 4 to 5 times.
Step 2, SOS Triggered: the alert is now live.
Step 3: the alert goes to your 3 trusted contacts.
Step 4, Grabbing Alert: contacts get a loud, unmissable alert with View and Call.
Step 5: recording starts automatically and uploads to the cloud.
Step 6: the recording is saved to the cloud every minute, so nothing is lost if the phone is damaged or switched off.
Step 7: the message carries your name, number, battery level, live location and active status.
Step 8: the nearest police station, ambulance and hospital are one tap away, along with 112.
Step 9: all 3 contacts see each other’s details, so they can act together.
Step 10, Pre-saved Contacts: 3 pre-saved numbers are shared for immediate help. You can add another number.

Step 11, You Also Receive It: everything sent to your trusted contacts is sent to you too — location, details, device status, emergency numbers and the recording — along with whether each contact has received and read the alert.
Step 12: at panic time everything is ready — call, live location, recording, battery, emergency numbers and contact details.
Step 13: help reaches faster and lives are safer. PUKAAR — when you need, we notify.
